cohort: 18,290 women who gave birth to 18,118 live-born children in five hospitals in Suriname, covering 86% of all births in the country during 2016 and 2017.
finding: The study revealed substantial inequities in maternal and perinatal health outcomes across different ethnic groups in Suriname.
mod_finding: The national cesarean section rate was 24% and varied significantly by ethnicity, being lower in Maroon women (17%) compared to Hindustani women (32%).
